inspiration: Font families as material variants: one serif and one tiny set, then the same glyph shapes re-coloured as wood, metal, gold and serpent-theme. For our HUD titles, use one set of our own letterforms and three palettes, each with a dark rim and one bright top-edge highlight.

Paperdoll layering: equipped items are separate shape layers that follow body frames, so a helmet or cloak swaps without redrawing the figure. For our armour, use one layer per slot with anchor points, and keep each item's palette on its own layer.

A status-bar icon band: one small pictogram per function (backpack, food, combat, keyring, disk, a jawbone) on a fixed grid. For our HUD, one icon grammar, one lit edge, one pixel grid, and our own function list.

Retro intro texture: the intro is built from short static bursts, a monitor slap and a shot over quiet gaps (per file names; not listened to). Recreate the idea with our own noise bursts over a low hum and a few tonal stings, with our own sound design.

Menu and slider art as small pieces: checkmark background, slider, scrollbar and a hp bar as separate small shapes that a UI draws from. For our menus, build a small shared kit of pieces at fixed sizes rather than one large image per screen.
Localisation as keyed text files: UI strings sit in one file per language with keys, and a short quotes file for the team. The structure is worth copying; the strings are not.

briefs.label: Engraved title font set
briefs.why: one glyph set in three material looks reads as a carved title on stone, wood or gold; the material does the work, not new letters
keep: one glyph set re-coloured per material
titles that name a material (wood, metal, gold)
a serif and a plain sans pair for body and headings
change: our own letterforms, not runic ones
faction palettes instead of wood, metal and gold
a wear or scratch pattern on top of the colour

briefs.label: Slot-layered armour
briefs.why: each equipped item is its own layer keyed to the body frame, so the character can change look without a new full sprite
keep: one layer per slot with anchor frames
change: our own slot names and layer order
a clear silhouette per armour tier

keep: short noise bursts over a quiet hum
single stings in the silent gaps
a sudden hard hit to close a beat
change: original sound design, not these clips
a different theme than an old monitor
